STATEMENT OF WORK
Forloop — Customer Insights Dashboard for Calderwick Retail Group

1. Project Overview

Forloop will design, build, and deliver a Customer Insights Dashboard for
Calderwick Retail Group, enabling Calderwick's marketing and operations teams to visualize
customer behavior, sales trends, and inventory turnover in a single, real-time interface.
This Statement of Work covers the full engagement from data integration through
production launch, over an estimated 8-week timeline.

Forloop is an AI engineering company: we design, build and operate data and machine-learning
products for enterprise clients. This engagement applies the same data-platform and analytics
practices to Calderwick's reporting needs.

2. Team

- Sofia Martins — Project Manager
- Elena Ruiz — Engineering Lead
- Marcus Chen — Backend Engineer
- Priya Patel — Frontend Engineer
- David Osei — QA Engineer
- Nirmal Babu — Delivery Manager
- Ram Anandkumar — Technical Director
- Rucheek — Infrastructure Engineer

3. Scope of Work

Phase 1: Discovery & Data Integration (Weeks 1-3)

- Elena Ruiz will lead a technical discovery session with Calderwick's IT team to catalog
  existing data sources (POS system, inventory database, CRM exports).
- Marcus Chen will build a secure ETL pipeline to ingest daily sales and inventory data
  from Calderwick's POS system into our analytics warehouse. This is foundational and must
  be completed before any dashboard visualizations can be built.
- Marcus Chen will implement a nightly sync job to pull customer records from Calderwick's
  CRM, deduplicating against existing records.
- Elena Ruiz will design the analytics data schema (fact and dimension tables) to support
  the dashboard's planned metrics.
- Ram Anandkumar will coordinate with Calderwick's IT team to set up secure VPN access to
  the staging POS replica, needed for the ETL pipeline and dashboard testing.
- Sofia Martins will deliver a data mapping document to Calderwick for sign-off by end of
  Week 2.

Phase 2: Dashboard Development (Weeks 3-6)

- Priya Patel will build the dashboard's core layout and navigation shell, following
  Calderwick's brand guidelines.
- Priya Patel will implement the Sales Trends view, showing daily/weekly/monthly revenue
  broken down by store location. This depends on the ETL pipeline being complete.
- Priya Patel will implement the Customer Segmentation view, allowing Calderwick to filter
  customers by purchase frequency and average order value. This depends on the CRM sync
  job being complete.
- Priya Patel will implement the Inventory Turnover view, highlighting slow-moving and
  out-of-stock SKUs by location.
- Marcus Chen will build the backend API endpoints powering each dashboard view, with
  response caching for performance.
- Elena Ruiz will implement role-based access control so Calderwick's regional managers
  only see data for their own stores.

Phase 3: Testing & Launch (Weeks 6-8)

- David Osei will conduct end-to-end QA across all three dashboard views, testing against
  real Calderwick data samples.
- David Osei will perform load testing on the backend API to confirm it can handle
  Calderwick's expected 200 concurrent users.
- Sofia Martins will coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT) with a pilot group of five
  Calderwick store managers, targeting Week 7.
- Elena Ruiz will address any critical bugs surfaced during UAT before production sign-off.
- Sofia Martins will deliver a training session and user guide to Calderwick's staff ahead
  of go-live.
- Nirmal Babu will oversee final delivery coordination and sign-off with Calderwick's
  stakeholders ahead of go-live.
- The team will deploy the dashboard to Calderwick's production environment, targeting a
  go-live date of the end of Week 8.

4. Timeline

Engagement duration: 8 weeks from kickoff. Data mapping sign-off due end of Week 2. UAT
targeted for Week 7. Production go-live targeted for end of Week 8.

source_documents.content:
MEETING MINUTES
Forloop / Calderwick Retail Group — Weekly Sync, Week 3

Attendees: Sofia Martins, Elena Ruiz, Marcus Chen, Priya Patel, David Osei, Nirmal Babu,
Ram Anandkumar, Rucheek

Summary:

- Marcus Chen confirmed the ETL pipeline for daily sales and inventory data from the POS
  system is complete and has been running successfully in production for the past three
  days.
- The nightly CRM sync job is done and verified - deduplication is working correctly
  against the last two years of customer records.
- Elena Ruiz reported the analytics data schema is finalized and reviewed with the team.
- The data mapping document was delivered to Calderwick and signed off on schedule.
- Priya Patel has started on the dashboard's core layout and navigation shell; expects to
  have it ready for internal review by early next week.
- Priya Patel flagged that the Sales Trends view is currently blocked - Calderwick's IT team
  has not yet granted VPN access to the staging POS replica, so live data can't be pulled
  in for testing. Ram Anandkumar reported he has escalated the access request with
  Calderwick's IT team twice this week with no resolution yet. Sofia Martins will follow up
  with Calderwick's IT contact today.
- Marcus Chen has started building the backend API endpoints for the dashboard views,
  prioritizing the Sales Trends endpoint first once the VPN access blocker clears.
- New item: Calderwick's operations lead requested an additional view during a check-in
  call - a Returns & Refunds trend view, broken down by store and reason code. Sofia
  Martins added this to scope as a Phase 2 addition. Priya Patel will own building this
  view once the core three views are stable.
- David Osei has begun drafting QA test plans for the Sales Trends and Customer
  Segmentation views ahead of Phase 3.
- Nirmal Babu noted this blocker is now a delivery risk against the Week 8 go-live and
  wants it reviewed at the leadership level rather than only tracked at the working level.
- Given the VPN access blocker is affecting the critical path, Nirmal Babu, Ram
  Anandkumar, and Rucheek agreed to reconvene early next week specifically to review
  whether Calderwick's IT team has resolved it, rather than waiting for the regular weekly
  sync.
